CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  November 14, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Lisa Massaro, Amy Wong, Ron Sahu, Scott Chan, Xana Hermosillo

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 9-19-24 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  The Environmental Sustainability Commission will discuss action items for the next meeting.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please
  limit all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior
  to the meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business
  of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5)
  minutes.

  VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, January 9, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

 If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the
Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact David Dolphin, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Special Meeting on September 19, 2024

  The special meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
  order at 6:00 p.m. on September 19, 2024.

•  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Wong, Sahu, Chan, Hermosillo
  Commission Members Absent: Massaro – Notified Commission Previously

  Commission members gave self-introductions.

  Staff Present:David Dolphin – Commission Secretary
  Latoya Waters – Environmental Compliance Specialist
  Lucy Garcia – Asst. City Manager
  Katie Martel – Sustainability Management Analyst
  ESA Representative - Stephanie Cadena

  Members of the Public
  Sandy Lee
  Jennifer Ng

•  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES FROM
  The meeting minutes will not be approved from the 3/14/24 meeting since none of the
  current Commission members present were appointed at that time.

  Absent: Massaro
  Commissioner Hermosillo self-nominated for the position of Vice President.
  Vote:  Ayes: Sahu, Chan, Wong
  Nays: None
  Absent: Massaro

   ITEM #II
Commissioner Sahu will now chair the meeting as President

•  UPDATE ITEMS

  Staff was notified the Update Items from the prior meeting was not included in the
  agenda packet and confirmed a copy will be emailed to the Commission.

  Verbally provided by City staff:

  Environmental Sustainability Commission Special Meeting- September 19, 2024
  Update Items

  1. Bike & Pedestrian Plans & Sustainability Plan
  Updates provided by Lucy Garcia:
  • March 2024 – Council adopted the Bike and Pedestrian Improvement Plan
  after two years of development.
  • Variety of recommendations for infrastructure and programming and
  everything that aligns with the active transportation elements and
  associated costs.
  • Staff received early direction from the City Council to secure funding for
  improvements and to reassign $14.4 M that was allocated to a project
  under measure R mobility improvement projects for the 710 FWY.
  • Went to metro board to request reallocation July 2024. Request was
  approved by Metro board. Currently waiting for the funding agreement so
  we can partake in the other efforts that go with implementing the plan.
  • The City is going to utilize more than $14.4 M to implement the projects.
  Looking at a variety of resources. Most recently applied for a grant
  through Caltrans under their Active Transportation Program. Also, to help
  facilitate a good part of the bike improvements. This $14.4M hope to
  initially place one of the pedestrian improvements which the Council
  requested to prioritize.
  Questions
  Wong – Is the $14.4 M the total the City applied for in regards to funding?
  Garcia- It’s what we had available under our Measure R
  allocations. Everything else is preassigned to other projects.
  Please provide examples of the pedestrian improvements the City
  would like to prioritize.
  Garcia- There are specifically 8 pedestrian locations identified in the
  plan. A map is included which includes a variety of tool boxes to help,
  facilitate traffic calming, improve safety, improve visibility, and the traffic
  active transportation options that the City are seeking. Such as;
  pedestrian enhancements, curb extensions, high visibility crosswalks,
  advanced pedestrian intervals. During the design and engineering phase,
  more details will be provided and options that will be selected.

  Page 2 of 10
   ITEM #II
  Sahu- What projects were taken away now that the $14.4M was reallocated?
  Garcia – The City had $241M in allocations for Measure R. Expected to
  submit all of the projects along with rough estimates for costs. Metro
  expects the estimates so they can program their cash expectations for each
  of the jurisdictions. The $14.4M came from the street widening project;
  Fremont between Valley and Mission.
  Is that widening project going to occur?
  Garcia – It is not going to occur. When the request to solicit proposals
  came to the Council, they were not thrilled with certain components
  related to the specifications. The project called for eliminating a median
  with greenscape and some of the irregular turn pockets.
  Is it safe to say that some projects to widen Fremont between Valley
  and Mission could have occurred but under Council direction, the
  funds will be used for the first phase of the Bike and Pedestrian
  Plan?
  Garcia- Correct. The original $241 M allocated was intended to focus on
  capacity type projects. The Metro Board allowed for the integration of
  active transportation projects.
  Is the $14.4 going to be consumed totally by the 8 pedestrian
  locations?
  Garcia- Yes, but will only be certain once design and engineering are
  completed. The Bike Plan calculated $20M.

2. Organic Waste Recycling Program

  •  Advertising & Marketing RFP - On August 26, 2024, the Council
  approved a contract with City Fabrick in the amount of $60,000 to support
  the City’s organics and food recovery collections programs in accordance
  with SB1383. As part of the consultant’s work, they will be taking a deep
  dive into how the public can properly dispose of organic waste. The firm
  is an environmentally-focused nonprofit organization with expertise in
  community engagement and multilingual marketing. In fact, they have
  strong ties to the San Gabriel Valley, having worked with various cities
  and the Go Human campaign under Southern California Association of
  Governments (SCAG). They will be accommodating both traditional and
  innovative outreach with an emphasis on reaching our diverse community.
  The costs associated with this contract are covered by grant funds received
  from the CA Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery. A kick
  off meeting with the consultant was planned for 9/18/24 to discuss specific
  next steps.
  •  Alhambra Recycles Event - The Biannual Alhambra Recycles Event
  returns this Fall on Saturday, September 28th. Alhambra residents are
  invited to collect compost, shred documents, and recycle electronic waste
  from 8AM to 12PM at Granada Park. The first 130 attendees will receive a
  free Fosselman’s Ice Cream gift certificate. Additional information can be
  found at www.cityofalhambra.org/recycle.

  Page 3 of 10
   ITEM #II
  •  Scholarship – The City Council commended the winners of the Third
  Annual Environmental Scholarship Award at the regular scheduled
  Council Meeting on July 22nd. Republic Services joined with the City of
  Alhambra to award five scholarships of $1,000 to Alhambra students.
  Each finalist submitted an essay based on the theme of environmental
  stewardship.
  • Bins for Business – As part of the Alhambra Recycles Campaign, the City
  of Alhambra is proud to offer free indoor recycling and organics
  containers to Alhambra businesses to jumpstart their recycling program.
  Qualified Alhambra businesses may receive up to 2 blue containers for
  recyclables and 2 green containers for organic waste, along with literature,
  stickers, biodegradable bags, and staff training. Additional information
  can be found at www.cityofalhambra.org/recycle.
  • Camp Alhambra Goes Green— City staff and Republic Services have
  been actively involved in the City’s Summer Camp program, offering fun
  and engaging games to educate campers about the benefits of recycling,
  conservation, and other sustainability initiatives. Residents are encouraged
  to stay updated on activities by following the City’s social media accounts.
Questions
Wong- Can you repeat the name of the firm?
  Dolphin – City Fabrick.
  Do you know what City Fabrick’s outreach looks like?
  Martel- City Fabrick is a local non-profit that work with a lot of public
  agencies. They are based out of Long Beach and participated in some of
  the campaigns around pedestrian safety with the Southern California
  Association of Governments. Most recently worked with the City of
  Monterey Park on their Parks Plan update. Their outreach is innovative
  and creative and really count on the face-to-face interaction and being
  able to reach out to residents to get involved. Examples include; get out
  the vote campaign where a photo booth was set up to interact with
  residents and creating a wall for residents to write how they perceive
  pedestrian safety in their community. They also have the ability to do the
  multi-lingual engagement needed for the project.

Sahu- In regards to the organic waste recycling program compliance with
  SB1383. What will this company do that Recycling isn’t currently
  implementing? Is it going to be geared toward residents at increasing
  their awareness of organic recycling or more focused on businesses
  and restaurants? Is it working in partnership with Republic services?
  Martel- Under SB 1383 there were some allocations from Cal Recycle.
  The first allocation was for the educational campaign which created
  compost Charlie and outreach materials. The City needed something
  Alhambra specific for our residents and Republic is not Alhambra
  specific. The second round of funding focused on getting the message out
  on the ground level.
  The actual physical separation of waste lies with Republic?
  Martel- Yes

  Page 4 of 10
   ITEM #II
  After City Fabrick does the outreach, should the City see an uptick in
  actual collections and diversions into something compostable? Is that
  a fair goal?
  Martel- It’s a metric that will be measured along with others to monitor
  how the educational campaign is resonating with residents.

  Hermosillo - Is there a possibility for renters to get the compost buckets?
  Martel- The City does have some inventory but we will look
  further to providing residents with the buckets.

  Chan- Is it possible to get some samples from Fabrick regarding what they
  have planned for multi-lingual outreach and what was done in
  Monterey Park?
  Martel- We’ll engage with Fabrick and start the contract in the later part
  of this year and strategize the first couple of months.

  Staff advised that an update on the item be provided at future meetings.

3. Safe Clean Water Program (SCWP)
The City has submitted an application to fund the Green Street Demonstration Project
on Main St.
  • Application for construction costs was submitted to the Safe Clean Water
  Program (SCWP) FY 2024-25 call for projects by the deadline, July 31,
  2023. The project was presented to the Upper LA River Watershed Area
  Steering Committee on February 7, 2024. The project was tentatively
  approved for funding and awaiting final approval from LA County Board
  of Supervisors.
  • A contract has been awarded for the design of the Burke Heritage Park
  and Marengo Yard Stormwater Capture Project. Notice to proceed was
  issued May 2024.
  Questions
  Sahu- For clarification, the Green Street project on West Main Street
  as well as the Burke Heritage Park project were awarded to CWE
  for design?
  Dolphin – Correct.

  Wong- CWE stands for Craftwater Engineering?
  Dolphin – CWE is not Craftwater Engineering.

4. Turf Replacement Rebate
The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) has submitted the
application for the DWR Drought Relief Grant to provide assistance to its member
agencies to fund a turf replacement rebate program. Unfortunately, the grant was not
approved.

Staff advised the grant was highly competitive and other agencies were able to prove
larger water savings.

  Page 5 of 10
   ITEM #II
  Questions
  Wong - Is the City looking for other grant sources to fund the program?
  Dolphin – The City hasn’t discussed the options as of yet. The grant was
  submitted by SGVMWD which covers 4 water agencies. The item may be
  discussed at a future board meeting.

  Sahu – For clarification, the City itself did not apply for the grant, the
  application was submitted by the SGVMWD on behalf of the water
  agencies. Can we apply for these grants directly since we get
  roughly 80% of our well water from well water?
  Dolphin –The SGVMWD may have internal funding but we can look to
  apply directly for grants just as we did for the AMI water meters.

•  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE

  ESA provided an update for the Commission (PowerPoint presentation)
  Stephanie Cadena, Urban Planner- Working with City staff over the last year on the
  plan.

  Questions
  Chan –From the 530 plus folks engaged during this outreach phase, share
  what that looked like regarding multi-lingual outreach? How many
  were in different languages? How many took advantage of the virtual
  events? In the questionnaire, which Chinese was used, simplified or
  traditional?
  Cadena- A lot of responses for the questionnaire were received in Spanish
  and Mandarin. Did not receive many at the in-person workshop.
  Interpreters were present but a few used the service. Most of the feedback
  was from the questionnaire. Thought the Chinese was simplified but will
  check to see which one was used.
  For the website and social media outlets, are there in language assets
  that will be put on the website.
  Cadena- For flyers and questionnaires, they will be in multiple languages
  but don’t know about the City’s website.
  Garcia- The City will evaluate what can be done.
  Comment from Chan – There are different translation companies that
  can do the translations on the back end so don’t have to keep
  updating the page. There are concerns with the loss of information
  through Google Translate.

  Wong- When is the deadline for feedback for this period of observation?
  Cadena – Thinking to do outreach for October and November, maybe
  December, trying to avoid the holidays. No set date range as of yet.
  Is there a sense of priority in terms of what you are presenting?
  Cadena – Green space was done first since it was the one that seemed
  most important. The rest are just ordered randomly. Will ask what is

  Page 6 of 10
   ITEM #II
  most important to the City and community members and Commission
  members.
  Comment- LA County Parks needs assessment is helpful to determine the
  areas in the City of Alhambra that has the highest need for green space.

Hermosillo-  Comment- Moor Field is listed as a park within 10-minute
  walking distance from my home, but it is not accessible to the
  public.
  • Agree with Commissioner Wong to prioritize equity around
  the project area.
  • Poor air quality is an important issue and we should
  achieve multi-benefits from our actions.
  • Black soot covers areas near the train tracks.
  • More trees to provide shade for cooling and improve air
  quality.
  • Other cities have the cooling effect.
  • The types of trees that we have in the City are not shade
  producing (crape myrtle trees).
  • Pedestrians are walking for necessity and fitness.
  • Attend farmers market multiple times because some
  residents are not there every week.
  Cadena- Information was received from the Trust for Public Land
  data set. Didn’t check to see if the parks were accessible.

Wong- Comment- A lot of the outreach can be achieved in partnership with
  community-based organizations; API Forward Movement, Active SGV,
  Tree People. These organizations can assist with finding funding. The
  questionnaire should allow participants to provide examples of success
  stories around sustainability.

Chan - For community engagement round 2- what metrics are you trying to
  achieve? What does success look like? Are there certain groups or
  numbers you are trying to reach?
  Cadena- ESA met with a lot of stakeholders in the workshop and now
  we’re trying to back to them one on one and really dive into the material.
  Priority is getting information from people that didn’t participate, i.e.,
  students. Seeking a diverse input; no set number in mind. The goal is to
  attempt to do more than last time.
  Concerned a lot on non-English speaking folks are not going to be
  reached. For long term future, this needs to be put in the forefront.

Sahu- The plan should be actionable. The Commission will help present the plan.
  The stakeholders include residents, home owners, renters and
  landlords, small businesses restaurant and non- restaurant, municipal
  entities. The plan should provide guidance for all City Departments.
  Currently, on road transportation with electric vehicle turn out is handled

  Page 7 of 10
   ITEM #II
  by the State. The City should make the incremental difference
  between what the State and Federal government does.
  What is the average carbon footprint for an Alhambra citizen and
  what is it in relation to the average state citizen?
  • City opted for 50% renewable energy; why not take it higher.
  Should be data driven; city specific data.
  • City does not do inventory of private trees. Cutting down trees to
  build adu’s.
  • Bring more data from other plans from the city to bring into the
  process.
  • Actionable and implementation should be driven by the user
  should make it more helpful. What can we do as citizens; short list
  or big list.
  • Minor issues; for questionnaires note if they previously responded;
  need new people.
  • City had 700 watch captains- pitch to council to strengthen the ties
  with the community. You will get a lot more information from
  these watch captains. APD has the information to send to them.
  • Higher quality response. Lead while getting input to make it
  effective. Indoor air quality is a big determination of people’s
  health. The two biggest long-term issues are cooking using gas,
  fragrances and odors.
  • Some point economic sustainability has its own challenges and
  should be addressed separately. Advise council take ownership.
  The City has data on the housing stock and age which can be used
  to help with the plan.

Hermosillo-  For transportation, the City should push for ACT buses to run more
  frequently with longer hours more places. Renters don’t have control
  over the action items; therefore, we should find ways to communicate with
  the landlords. Example, single pane windows cause us to run the air
  conditioner 24 hours a day, 7days a week.

  Wong – Get inspiration and ideas from neighboring cities. Example – Pasadena is
  a huge difference with shade and tree canopy. Have we contacted these
  cities?
  Cadena- Not directly. The information was received through meetings and
  other examples. Other models will be investigated.
  Sahu – The City should develop the best plan that is useful and actionable.
  Look for partnerships to become successful and set high expectations.

  Chan – The next phase should include more input from students. AUSD could
  provide the support.
  Garcia – The City meets with AUSD quarterly to relay the efforts of the
  Sustainability Plan; encouraging partnership with the schools. More trees
  are wanted on school campuses.

  Page 8 of 10
   ITEM #II
  Sahu - With neighborhood watches, there is a net benefit of trust building with
  the citizens and their government. Especially in communities where
  citizens are trained to not deal with government because think it may be
  troublesome.

•  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Sandy Lee - Expressed interest in getting involved with the Commission through
  volunteering and as a community task force leader. Sandy attended the
  sustainability plan workshop but found out no one followed up to get involved.
  She is very interested in organics recycling and would like to present to the
  Commission alternatives that are available besides hauling away food scraps. At
  the last Alhambra Recycles event, a soil scientist tested the soil and discovered no
  live microbes and the smell of manure. Sandy would like to be a resource, and
  has experience in industrial organics recycling, conversion, and transformation
  specifically at the Rose Bowl and will do the same at the golf course and
  Almansor Park.

  Jennifer Ng – Echoed the sentiments of the Commission that we do have a lot of
  community knowledge.
  • It is important to touch basis and see what’s happening in the community. A
  lot of community members are not aware of what’s going on but wait for
  someone to present them with the information. Going above the
  neighborhood watch by using community leaders to share information is
  necessary.
  • It can take years for any changes to occur on the ACT bus routes. The routes
  need to be changed due to the increased development in the City.
  • Some things are attached to environmental sustainability that we don’t think
  about like historic preservation.
  • Another source of outreach to the community is to sign up to receive emails
  from the City on upcoming Commission meetings and agenda items.
  • Classes at the library are important to help the community learn about
  sustainability.
  • Trees are being stressed because they are over trimmed by the City’s
  contractor which causes a decrease in tree canopy. The number of trees on
  private property needs to be increased.
  • Grey water needs to be allowed for use in the City. A lot of water is going to
  waste that could be used to water trees and vegetation.
  • If grass is removed from City property to install native vegetation, the City
  should pay for it. A rebate is needed to assist residents with removing grass
  because it can get expensive. Education is important as well.

  Commissioner Sahu commented - we must be careful about turf replacement. It
  has a positive effect on water savings but detrimental effect on heat island effect

  Page 9 of 10
   ITEM #II
  and human health indicators. The Commission will attempt to make data driven
  decisions.

•  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Commissioner Chan expressed her excitement with being part of the Commission.
  Commissioner Sahu thanked staff and ESA for participation in the meeting and
  mentioned in order to obtain good data, outreach must be done right and not rushed.

•  ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner Sahu motioned to adjourn the meeting at 7:59 PM.
